source.paraphrase: An error-handling middleware takes four arguments. Express selects it by arity, so a three-argument function is ordinary middleware and never receives the error.

invariants.why: A broken error signature leaves the app with no error middleware: the handler never runs and the failure surfaces as a hang or a default HTML page.
invariants.fixHint: Give the handler four parameters (err, req, res, next) and register it with app.use after the routes.
invariants.avoid: Renaming err to error, or switching arrow to function, does not add the missing parameter. Arity is what Express reads.

source.paraphrase: Express JSON and urlencoded parsers enforce a default 100kb size limit. An explicit limit is an optional project policy.

invariants.why: A missing explicit limit does not mean an unbounded parser; the documented default remains active.
invariants.fixHint: Pass a limit option such as express.json({ limit: "100kb" }). Raise it per route only where a large payload is legitimate.
invariants.avoid: The default 100kb cap is valid. Syntax cannot determine the appropriate per-route limit.

source.paraphrase: An upload endpoint without limits or a file filter accepts files of any size and type. The disk and the downstream consumer pay for whatever the caller sends.

invariants.why: Unbounded uploads fill the disk and smuggle executables or archives into a pipeline that expected an avatar.
invariants.fixHint: Configure multer with limits (fileSize, files) and a fileFilter that accepts only the mime types the feature needs.
invariants.avoid: A dest or storage option only chooses where files land. It does not bound size, count, or type.
